entries.title: Bears report No. 18: Ben Johnson has 'bad feeling' after Bengals loss
entries.summary: <p>Breaking down the Bears’ 27-9 loss to the Bengals at Paycor Stadium:</p><h3><b>Slow start</b></h3><p>Caleb Williams went 2-for-5 for 28 yards Saturday. The rest of his teammates weren’t much better.</p><p>At halftime, Bears coach Ben Johnson barked at his team about their penalties and performance on third down on both sides of the ball. The Bears finished with 11 penalties for 81 yards. They went 2-for-14 on third down and their defense went 6-for-13.</p><p>“It doesn’t matter whether it’s the preseason or not,” Johnson said, “it’s a bad feeling in that locker room after the game when you lose, especially like that.”</p><h3><b>New play-callers</b></h3><h3></h3><p>One week after he let receivers coach Antwaan Randle-El call offensive plays in the second, head coach Ben Johnson handed off those duties to tight ends coach Jim Dray.</p><p>Al Harris, the team’s defensive backs coach, called defensive plays in the second half. Harris spent five years with the Cowboys, the last as an assistant head coach, before joining Ben Johnson’s staff last year.</p><h3><b>Injury update</b></h3><p>Linebacker Nephi Sewell left the game on a cart with a knee injury. His brother and fellow Bears linebacker, Noah Sewell, is on the physically-unable-to-perform list while he recovers from an Achilles’ tendon injury.</p><p><b>What’s next</b><br>After two days off, the Bears return to Halas Hall to practice Tuesday.<br>— Patrick Finley<br></p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: Maren Haile-Selassie scores in Fire's 1-1 draw against the Red Bulls
entries.summary: <p>HARRISON, N.J.— Cameron Harper scored late in the second half after subbing in a minute earlier and the New York Red Bulls rallied for a 1-1 draw with the Fire on Saturday night.</p><p>Harper replaced Julian Hall in the 85th minute then used assists from Eric Maxim-Choupo and Omar Valencia to score in the 86th. It was his first goal in his fourth appearance this season.</p><p>Maren Heile-Selassie used assists from defender Viktor Radojević and Jonathan Bamba in the 38th minute to score his fourth goal and give Chicago a 1-0 lead that stood through halftime.</p><p>It was the first assist for Radojević in his third career start and 10th appearance.</p><p>Ethan Horvath had four saves for New York (7-9-5) to help end a two-match skid.</p><p>Chris Brady saved five shots for Chicago (11-6-3), now 2-2-2 in its last six matchups with the Red Bulls.</p><p>Chicago saw a three-match winning streak in league play end. The Fire had won six in a row in all competitions for the first time since their debut season in 1998.<br></p>

entries.title: Want to help northwest Indiana storm victims? How to support recovery efforts from Chicago
entries.summary: <p>As Indiana residents continue to recover from recent storms and power outages, organizations across Gary and the surrounding area are providing food, shelter and other resources to those impacted.</p><p>While power has been restored for over 340,000 residents, thousands of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/08/21/gary-storm-victims-fill-generators-at-a-gas-station-watch-dvds-in-car-eat-hot-lunch-at-a-school" target="_blank" ><u>NIPSCO customers</u></a> <a class="Link" href="https://www.nipsco.com/outages/power-outages" target="_blank" >remained without electricity</a> as of Saturday, two a weeks after strong storms battered northwest Indiana. </p><p>Chicagoans looking to help from afar can donate money and supplies or volunteer with organizations providing relief to residents.</p><p>Here are some organizations helping residents recover and how the public can support their efforts.</p><p><b>Catholic Charities  </b></p><p>Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Gary and Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Chicago are working to address resident needs, including food, clothing, housing assistance, and other resources. Chicagoans who would like to donate to Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Gary Storm Relief Fund can donate at<a class="Link" href="givesmart.com/events/QeW/" target="_blank" > givesmart.com/events/QeW/</a></p><p><b>Flourish Church and Flourish Community Hub</b></p><p>Flourish Church and Flourish Community Hub are seeking donations of dry goods and volunteers to provide resources to residents affected by the storms.</p><p>The organization plans to hold a Family Rest & Resource Sunday despite <a class="Link" href="https://www.facebook.com/flourishchurchnwi" target="_blank" ><u>being without power</u></a>.</p><p>Flourish Community Hub accepts one-time and monthly monetary <a class="Link" href="https://flourishcommunityhub.org/get-involved/" target="_blank" ><u>donations</u></a> and offers other ways to contribute, including volunteering,</p><p>Raydia Martin, assistant director for the organization, said the most urgent needs are non-perishable dry goods, bottled water and baby care items like wipes and diapers.</p><p>Some families are still without power and could use generators, Martin said.</p><p>"Assistance will still be needed after the storm," she said. "Even before the storm, Gary was a high-need area."</p><p><b>Food Bank of Northwest Indiana</b></p><p>The Food Bank of Northwest Indiana announced on its Facebook page that it had recently experienced significant <a class="Link" href="https://www.facebook.com/FoodBankofNorthwestIndiana" target="_blank" ><u>internet issues</u></a> for multiple days, preventing it from connecting with the community and agencies to gauge need.</p><p>The food bank is also seeking volunteers to help serve the community at mobile markets.</p><p>Those interested in donating can do so by visiting the <a class="Link" href="https://foodbanknwi.org/donate-to-foodbank/" target="_blank" ><u>food bank’s website</u></a>, contacting Natalie Krivas at 219-980-1777 (extension 315), or via email at nkrivas@foodbanknwi.org.</p><p><b>Gary Muslim Center</b></p><p>The Gary Muslim Center is raising money to provide emergency relief to families affected by the recent storms. As of Saturday evening, the fundraiser had collected more than $28,000 from 473 donations toward a $35,000 goal, up from its original $25,000 goal.</p><p>The center said donations will help provide clean water, halal hot meals, gas cards, clothing, diapers, emergency housing, and household items.</p><p>People who prefer to donate supplies can contribute through an Amazon wish list, according to the GoFundMe <a class="Link" href="https://www.gofundme.com/f/uplifting-gary-through-faith-and-service?cdn-cache=0" target="_blank" ><u>fundraiser</u></a>.</p><p><b>Gary NAACP</b></p><p>The Gary Branch of the NAACP recently partnered with local organizations on storm-relief efforts and has used its social media pages to <a class="Link" href="https://www.facebook.com/NAACPGARY/" target="_blank" ><u>share resources</u></a>.</p><p>People looking for additional opportunities to help can follow the Gary Branch of the NAACP’s <a class="Link" href="https://www.naacpgary.org/" target="_blank" ><u>website</u></a> and social media pages, where the organization has been sharing storm recovery resources, community events and calls for donations and volunteers.</p><p><b>YWCA of Northwest Indiana</b></p><p>YWCA Northwest Indiana has offered free resources to residents affected by the outages, including hot meals and showers, and said the facility has access to power, according to a recent post from the <a class="Link" href="https://www.facebook.com/YWCANWI" target="_blank" ><u>organization</u></a>.</p><p>People who want to donate can do so through YWCA Northwest Indiana’s <a class="Link" href="https://ywcanwi.org/" target="_blank" ><u>website</u></a>.<br></p>

entries.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong’s leadoff home-run barrage showing just how dangerous he is at top of Cubs’ batting order
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE – Hot take incoming.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> have something very valuable in <b>Pete Crow-Armstrong</b> at the top of their lineup.</p><p>No duh, right?</p><p>Crow-Armstrong has been perhaps the best player in baseball this season, a true MVP candidate, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/05/cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-shohei-ohtani-nl-mvp-race-dodgers-playoffs-craig-counsell-shota-imanaga" >even in a world where <b>Shohei Ohtani</b> exists</a>.</p><p>But though he’s been doing remarkable things all season, his latest trick stood out.</p><p>His leadoff home run in Friday’s loss to the Mariners was his third such dinger in a four-game stretch, after he led off the bottom of the first inning with home runs in back-to-back games against the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> last week.</p><p>Friday’s blast came as the conclusion of a nine-pitch at-bat, in contrast to the first-pitch homers he belted against the Sox.</p><p>“The first at-bat of a road trip, having an eight-, nine-, 10-pitch at-bat like he did, to hit a homer and get us going,” second baseman <b>Nico Hoerner</b> said Saturday, “it’s a huge deal and sets the tone for everyone.”</p><p>Crow-Armstrong has been setting the tone a lot. He’s up to seven leadoff homers on the season, five shy of the single-season franchise record of 12, set by <b>Alfonso Soriano</b> in 2007.</p><p>“We’ve got probably the most dynamic player in baseball leading off,” third baseman <b>Alex Bregman</b> said Friday. “He can hit the ball out of the ballpark, he can steal bags, he can battle up and slap a good at-bat on you.”</p><p>Crow-Armstrong is under MVP consideration because of his all-around excellence this season, and leadoff walks have impressed his teammates just as much as his leadoff homers have, a dramatic evolution in his offensive game. He’s also flashed elite base-running ability.</p><p>He can do it all. And he can do it all right away, causing an instant problem for opponents as the top-of-the-order hitter.</p><p>“Pete has some of the traditional leadoff qualities in the speed and the impact on the bases, but also he’s just the hitter that we want up most right now,” Hoerner said. “He kind of fits both boxes.</p><p>“He’s been incredible.”</p><p><b>Happ homers, still struggling</b></p><p>Left fielder <b>Ian Happ</b> hit a clutch home run Friday, bringing the Cubs within a run with his eighth-inning blast.</p><p>But a day later, he was out of the team’s starting lineup with a left-handed starter on the mound.</p><p>While Happ showed what sort of impact he’s capable of making, that impact has been muted against lefties. He came into Saturday hitting just .158 against southpaws, and manager <b>Craig Counsell</b> continued <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/04/cubs-ian-happ-lineup-lefties-tyrone-taylor-mlb-trade-deadline-left-field-craig-counsell-kyle-tucker-dodgers-pitching-injuries" >his recent strategy of sitting Happ against a lefty starter</a> with eyes on bringing him to face righties later in the game.</p><p>Though Happ still had an .812 OPS against righties this season, his overall numbers have been dragged down by the results against lefties, and coming into Saturday, he was batting just .199 in his previous 63 games.</p><p>“He’s a passionate, competitive person,” Hoerner said of Happ. “Obviously, he wants to contribute at a really high level. But I’ve also seen him go through challenging stretches and come out the other side of them with versions of himself that can carry an offense with weeks on end.</p><p>“There’s no change in confidence with him.”</p><p><b>Bregman bombs</b></p><p>Think the Mariners are sick of Bregman?</p><p>Their former division rival from his many years with the Astros, Bregman came into this weekend’s series with 13 career homers against the M’s.</p><p>But that number is rising quickly, and after another day of home-run exploits Saturday in Washington, there are only three teams he’s homered against more often in his career: the Athletics, Rangers and Angels.</p>

entries.title: Bears' starting defense doesn't hold up well vs. Bengals' backups in preseason game
entries.summary: <p>CINCINNATI — With a mix of second- and third-stringers, the Bengals drove 67 yards for a field goal on their first possession against most of the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ first-team defense to begin their preseason game Saturday.</p><p>For a unit that has plenty of question marks three weeks ahead of the regular season, that sequence didn’t help.</p><p>Bengals coach Zac Taylor held out quarterback Joe Burrow and the rest of his starters on both sides of the ball, as well as 41-year-old backup Joe Flacco, which meant journeyman Josh Johnson got the start.</p><p>Johnson completed 7 of 10 passes for 55 yards and pushed the Bengals to the Bears’ 7-yard line before settling for Evan McPherson’s 25-yard field goal. His offensive line, comprised of four second-stringers and one from the third team, held up fine and did not allow a quarterback hit against the Bears’ starting defensive line of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2025/09/04/bears-de-montez-sweat-out-to-reassert-himself-as-elite-pass-rusher-but-more-so-he-wants-to-finally-win" >Montez Sweat</a>, Dayo Odeyingbo, Gervon Dexter and Kentavius Street.</p><p>The Bears’ starting defense performed much better in the joint practice Thursday, when it spent the day dealing with Burrow and the Bengals’ starters.</p><p>The Bears kept Dexter, Odeyingbo and rookie cornerback Malik Muhammad in for the Bengals’ second possession, but pulled the rest of their starters. Dexter broke into the backfield and flushed Johnson out of the pocket on second-and-10, but Johnson bought enough time to throw the ball away.</p><p>Odeyingbo hit Johnson as he looked to throw on third down, helping force an incomplete pass, and the Bears forced a three-and-out on that possession.</p><p>While the Bears were one of the top scoring teams in the NFL last season, their defense was inconsistent. They struggled to stop the run or generate a pass rush and finished 29th in total defense, but negated a lot of that by leading the league with 33 takeaways.</p>

entries.title: 34-year-old man sitting in SUV killed in Englewood shooting
entries.summary: <p>A 34-year-old man died late Saturday after he was shot multiple times in Englewood, Chicago police said.</p><p>The victim had been sitting inside a gray SUV in the 6200 block of May Street at about 9:16 p.m. when an unidentified gunman approached him on foot and fired shots before fleeing in an unknown direction, police said.</p><p>The man suffered gunshot wounds to the shoulder and abdomen, police said.</p><p>He was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center in critical condition before being pronounced dead.</p><p>Area 1 detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: Police warn residents of late-night armed robberies in Bronzeville, Lake Meadows
entries.summary: <p>Chicago police are alerting the public about multiple armed robberies that occurred in Bronzeville and Lake Meadows this month.</p><p>In each of the area's robberies, police said one to three assailants are believed to have approached victims at night, armed with guns and demanding their mobile phones.</p><p>Police in a news bulletin indicated the suspects ordered victims to unlock their phones before taking the devices and fleeing the scene on foot.</p><p>The areas where the reported robberies happened include:</p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" style="margin-top:0;margin-bottom:0;padding-inline-start:48px;" id="rte-853ae290-9ea4-11f1-849c-73a842070f9a"><li>400 block of East 32nd Street on Aug. 6 at 10:15 p.m. </li><li>400 block of East 32nd Street on Aug. 14 at 11:45 p.m.</li><li>3000 block of South State Street on Aug. 14 at 11:45 p.m.<br></li></ul><p>Police described the suspects as three men and one woman, all wearing hooded sweatshirts.</p><p>Area residents are urged to remain aware of their surroundings and report any suspicious activity immediately, police said. </p><p>Anyone with information is encouraged to contact Area 1 detectives at 312-747-8380 or submit an anonymous tip at CPDTIP.com and provide reference number P26-1-070.<br></p>

entries.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams struggles after coach decides offense 'needed that work'
entries.summary: <p>CINCINNATI — After all the offseason hype, anything but a stellar performance from Caleb Williams on Saturday night would have felt disappointing.</p><p>What Bears fans got in their first look at the starting quarterback Saturday, he was anything but stellar.</p><p>Playing against second- and third-string Bengals players, Williams went 2-for-5 for 27 yards and a 58.8 passer rating in his only drive during the Bears' 27-9 loss. The Bears settled for a 45-yard Cairo Santos field goal after Williams overthrew Colston Loveland near the goal line and later threw wide of receiver Rome Odunze.</p><p>That’s not close to 70%, the completion percentage that coach Ben Johnson has so publicly set for his quarterback. Sure, Williams played just seven snaps — and two more on plays that were penalized — but it’s possible to seize momentum in so short a time. The Packers’ Jordan Love played 11 snaps a night earlier, completed 71% of his passes and finished with a 134.5 passer rating.</p><p>So what did Williams gain, exactly?</p><p>“He gained nine more reps, I know that,” head coach Ben Johnson said.</p><p>The fact Williams played at all was a surprise. Johnson had been non-committal about Johnson playing, claiming he'd make the decision after the Bears and Bengals had a joint practice Thursday. The coach was annoyed by three illegal procedure issues in the first seven plays of practice, and thought the offense “needed that work” Saturday.</p><p>That work wasn’t particularly sharp.</p><p>“We understand it’s the preseason,” Williams said. “It’s not obviously counting, but it does matter. And so that’s something that we live by.”</p><p>Complicating matters was the fact that Tyson Bagent, the team's second-string quarterback, did not make the trip to Cincinnati after hurting his hamstring in the preseason opener. In the next game, the Bears should let Case Keenum handle that. He’s played 80 career games. That’s why he’s here — not to play in the regular season.</p><p>Johnson will undoubtedly want to see more from Williams in the three weeks before the Bears open in Carolina. That should be limited to practice, though.</p><p>Johnson scheduled his team to leave town for three nights two weeks in a row because he wanted them to find their groove in the practices, not the game. Johnson should focus on what Williams does against the Titans during practice in Nashville on Thursday — and not play him in the Bears’ final exhibition game Saturday. The injury risk isn’t worth it.</p><p>Williams, for his part, said he’s up for “whatever coach decides.”</p><p>On the first drive at Paycor Stadium, Williams didn’t have a single highlight throw, a stark contrast from the clips of him that were pumped through the NFL universe all offseason.</p><p>Ever since he launched the back-pedaling touchdown pass to Cole Kmet — in a game the tight end has to remind his own friends that the Bears actually lost — Williams has been one of the faces of the NFL. He was put on the cover of “Madden 27” and got NFL 100 votes. Jaguars coach Liam Coen even joked that he couldn’t go to the NFL’s web site without seeing “40 photos of Caleb Williams.”</p><p>Williams’ best pass was his first. After faking a toss right to running back Roschon Johnson, Williams rolled left and, with Cedric Johnson rushing toward him with his left hand in the air, hit Odunze is stride for 18 yards. He then wobbled a quick pass to Colston Loveland for 10 yards and a first down.<br>The next time he threw toward Loveland, Williams should have had a touchdown. Instead, he threw the ball too high for the tight end, who tumbled to the ground at the 3. Williams said the play called for him to throw the ball elsewhere but the Bengals had broken coverage that left Loveland open. Johnson reiterated that Williams shouldn’t have thrown the ball there.</p><p>Williams’ last pass to Odunze fell incomplete, despite the receiver’s pleas for a flag. Williams said he threw the ball wide of Odunze on purpose; at the last second he saw a linebacker that had dropped into coverage because the Bears kept a running back in to pass protect against a blitz, and he didn’t want to throw an interception.</p><p>Braxton Jones’ holding penalty before the incompletion to Loveland had the Bears facing first-and-20. They didn’t gain a yard on either of the next two plays.</p><p>“There’s not many calls that you can have for second-and-20 or third-and-20,” Williams said.</p><p>He’s supposed to be the great eraser, though, right?</p><p>The Bengals thought so little of Saturday night's exhibition that they started 40-year-old third-stringer Josh Johnson, who has played for 14 different NFL teams, a record for quarterbacks, plus stints with AAF’s San Diego Fleet and the XFL’s Los Angeles Wildcats.</p><p>Playing alongside fellow backups, Johnson marched the Bengals 62 yards on 14 plays on the opening drive against the Bears’ starting defense.<br>By then, Williams was on the sideline doing what he should have been doing — sitting down. And likely regretting that his in-game debut Saturday night didn’t go better.<br></p>

entries.title: Luis Castillo struggles again, Luis Robert Jr. hits two home runs in White Sox' 10-5 loss to Mets
entries.summary: <p>Luis Castillo struggled again and Luis Robert Jr. had his first multi-homer game in two years.</p><p>Yeah, it was a rough night for the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a>, who lost 10-5 to the Mets on Saturday.</p><p>In his fourth Sox start, Castillo only lasted 2 2/3 innings, giving up four<b> </b>runs and homers to Robert and Bo Bichette. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/01/chicago-white-sox-mariners-luis-castillo-seranthony-dominguez-prospects-nolan-jones-boston-smith-chris-getz" >Acquired Aug. 1 from the Mariners</a>, Castillo’s only completed five innings once and allowed five home runs with the Sox.</p><p>Brought in to be a veteran anchor and provide some experience to an otherwise-green staff trying to nail down a division title, Castillo has not yet justified the investment by general manager Chris Getz to grab him from Seattle. Other than his 10-strikeout game against the Reds, Castillo has lacked put-away stuff with the Sox.</p><p>Against the Mets, Castillo threw strikes on 51 of his 80 pitches but only struck out three. The Bichette and Robert home runs were both hit with two strikes, as was Carson Benge’s run-scoring single in the first.</p><p>“They were taking good at-bats. They were hitting a lot of foul balls,” Castillo said through a translator. “I was attacking the zone. The best part is that I’m feeling good.”</p><p>Robert was probably feeling even better. He homered twice in a game for the eighth time in his career and first since Aug. 16, 2024, when he was with the Sox.</p><p>Starting in left field for the third time in his career, Robert had trouble with the sun on Miguel Vargas’ first-inning shallow fly and let it drop for a single. Robert and the Mets recovered by retiring Vargas after he went too far rounding first base.</p><p>Then Robert flashed the power that once made him a tantalizing Sox prospect. In the third, Robert reached out to poke a 95.6 mph Castillo four-seam fastball to right-center field to give New York a 4-1 lead. As Robert rounded the bases, he was booed by many of the 30,705 in attendance.</p><p>“Yesterday, I felt a little weird hearing [the boos],” Robert said through a translator. “I felt it to be a little bit strange, but today it was pretty normal. Yesterday, I wasn’t expecting it but today it was pretty normal to hear.”</p><p>Robert made that trip again in the seventh, but even more emphatically.</p><p>Castillo was long gone, and Sox reliever Huascar Brazoban threw Robert a thigh-high 98 mph four-seam fastball over the heart of the plate. Robert launched it 417 feet to left with a 109 mph exit velocity and clearly enjoyed what he had done, watching the drive as he slowly began making his way to first base.</p><p>“It feels good to hit homers against any team, to be honest with you,” Robert said. “I will say it did feel good to hit the home runs here just because it was a stadium that I played so many games in my whole career.”</p><p>It was probably irritating to the Sox to see him hit two home runs, but his direct impact on their season will end when the Mets leave.</p><p>Castillo will be around longer and figure much more into how this season plays out. If he can recapture some of the form that made him a three-time All-Star, the Sox could have something. If not, then the rotation will still be short.</p><p>The Sox won’t be overhauling what -Castillo does, but simply working to get him at his best.</p><p>“As an athlete we have good days and bad days [and] it was a bad day today,” Castillo said. “That’s what I’m thinking.”<br></p>

entries.title: East St. Louis dominates the second half, ends Mount Carmel's 19-game winning streak
entries.summary: <p>NORMAL, Ill.—College scholarship offers don’t win games. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/08/18/mount-carmel-football-chicago-ihsa" >Mount Carmel has a historic number of college-bound players</a>, but the Caravan couldn’t find a way to beat East St. Louis on Saturday at Hancock Stadium.</p><p>Mount Carmel turned the ball over twice in one minute early in the fourth quarter, and the Flyers cashed both in for touchdowns and went on to win 42-23, snapping the Caravan’s 19-game winning streak.</p><p>“Losing sucks,” Mount Carmel coach Jordan Lynch said. “We have to grow as a program. We are lazy, undisciplined all over. It is Week 1 struggles for sure. When you play a team like that that is well-coached, that travels and plays the best of the best, it is a great challenge for your program. I have great respect for [East St. Louis coach Darren Sunkett].”</p><p>The Caravan have won four consecutive state championships and opened the season as the favorite to win Class 8A again. The Flyers play in Class 6A.</p><p>It should be noted that East St. Louis also has a load of college-bound players, including some of the most talented prospects in the country. Mount Carmel entered this matchup as a slight but not overwhelming favorite.</p><p>“[This win] means something,” Sunkett said. “We hear we couldn’t win. We had something to prove. We have been at state seven years in a row. Win or lose we were there. It is tough to win in the state of Illinois. We came out with a chip on our shoulder. We wanted to show that we could play with Mount Carmel and beat them.”</p><p>Both teams were without key players in the second half. East St. Louis was without running back Myson Johnson-Cook, an Auburn recruit. He had 12 carries for 88 yards in the first half but didn’t play in the second half.</p><p>“When Myson went down, it would have been easy to drop our heads,” Sunkett said. “[Ronnie Gomiller] came and said to put him in at running back.
